The world switches every 300 steps, and nothing the loop does changes the world or when inputs arrive. With sensory input alone the loop locks in on every seed. The question's five candidates are added as switches, each with its stated objection built in. The sensory candidate is split into its channel and exogenous capture. With all present the loop follows every switch, and no single removal makes it lock in. In the minimal loops, removing commitment before evidence, processing signals or exogenous capture makes the loop lock in. Removing an evidence channel (the senses, the body, testimony) leaves it blind, unless capture goes with it. Over 19 parameter variants, a loop with evidence avoided lock-in when it had one of those three anchors in 37 to 42 of 44 configurations per variant. The exceptions are stated. A fictional model, by construction; the numbers are of this model. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

The harmful seeds have large islands; the errors are order effects at the binding threshold. A post hoc predictor, threshold-front forcing (TFF), meets the pre-registered criterion on five fresh architectures (Spearman 0.64 against 0.48, AUC 0.94, recall 0.66, precision 0.11). The model is the assistant's. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

With the drive made to depend on the system's state (500 systems), the identities and the summed bound still hold, but a step's nostalgia is negative in 405, the summed nostalgia in 323, and the dissipation and the excess work in 6. In an 8-percept loop where the predictive partition is a sticky nuisance and the interventional partition is the context the action must match, the memory that keeps only the context is the cheapest that does the task by every cost measured; the policy that uses it changes its nostalgia from ln 2 to 0 and leaves its heat per step unchanged.
